title: The Port, the Palace and the Ashes: Pinochet from Valparaiso to Los Boldos
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Valparaíso, the birth on the hill
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Augusto Pinochet Ugarte is born in the port of Valparaíso, eldest of six children of a customs employee. The city he is born into is Chile's window on the Pacific, a place of cranes and funiculars and ships' manifests, where the business of the state is counting what comes ashore. There is no army in the family. He is baptized into the careful lower middle class of a republic that has not had a soldier in the palace for a generation. Ninety-one years later the same coast will hold his ashes, in a private house forty kilometres south, and no cemetery in the country will carry his name on a stone.
suggested_refs: The parish registers of Valparaíso for November 1915; the exact house of birth is not identified in any reachable source

stops.name: Santiago, the Escuela Militar on the third attempt
stops.date_confidence: contested. Spanish Wikipedia gives entry on 11 March 1933 after two failed attempts; English Wikipedia gives 1931. The 1933 date is used because it alone fits the December 1936 graduation and the September 1937 Chacabuco posting. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved.
stops.campa: Schooled inland at the Rafael Ariztía Institute in Quillota and then back in Valparaíso, he presents himself twice at the Escuela Militar in Santiago and is twice turned away. The third application takes. He enters as an infantry cadet at seventeen, into the neoclassical barracks near Parque O'Higgins that the school occupies long before its move to Las Condes. The Chile that trains him is a republic recovering from the collapse of the nitrate economy and from the short military governments of Ibáñez and Grove. The army he joins has already tasted the palace once and been sent back to barracks.
suggested_refs: The Balmaceda-era Escuela Militar building on Blanco Encalada, near Parque O'Higgins, the campus of his cadet years
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Escuela Militar del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins'

stops.name: Concepción, the Chacabuco Regiment
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month. He graduates 29 December 1936 and receives the rank of alférez on 1 January 1937; the day of the September posting is not fixed by any reachable source and is defaulted to the first.
stops.campa: He graduates at the end of 1936, takes the rank of alférez on the first day of 1937, and in September is posted south to the Chacabuco Regiment at Concepción, the coal and steel city on the Bío Bío. It is his first command of men. A short train ride away are the pits of Lota and Coronel, the most organized labour in Chile and already voting communist. He is twenty-one. The regiment's business is infantry drill; the province's business is a quarrel he will spend the rest of his life on one side of.
suggested_refs: The Chacabuco Regiment barracks at Concepción; the exact address is unverified and the pin is the city centre

stops.name: San Bernardo, the Infantry School and the Hiriart marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the marriage. The verified pool gives the place only as Chile; the stop is pinned at San Bernardo because that is where he was posted. The Infantry School posting itself is 1941, not the 1940 carried in some accounts.
stops.campa: By way of the Maipo Regiment at Valparaíso he reaches the Escuela de Infantería at San Bernardo, south of Santiago, and there Lieutenant Pinochet marries Lucía Hiriart Rodríguez, daughter of a Radical Party senator and interior minister. The marriage brings the customs clerk's son the one thing the army cannot issue him: a name inside the political class of the republic he serves. Five children will follow. She will outlive him by fifteen years and read his last public statement aloud for him. She dies at ninety-eight, under indictment over the money.
suggested_refs: The Escuela de Infantería at San Bernardo, where he is posted in 1941

stops.name: Arica, the Rancagua Regiment on the Peruvian line
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted to 1 January and carrying no evidentiary weight. Intervening postings at Iquique (Carampangue, 1945) and the Academia de Guerra (1949) rest on a single source and are tagged reconstruction there.
stops.campa: Promoted major, he takes up duties with the Rancagua Regiment at Arica, the desert city on the Peruvian border and the northernmost garrison of the republic. The frontier posting is where Chilean officers learn geopolitics as a physical fact: a long thin country pressed between the cordillera and the sea, holding by force of arms two provinces taken from two neighbours in the last century. Behind him are staff years at the Academia de Guerra, which is the making of him. He is not a battlefield soldier and never will be. Chile fights no war in his lifetime.
suggested_refs: The Rancagua Regiment garrison at Arica, on the frontier taken from Peru in 1883

stops.name: Quito, the Ecuadorean War Academy
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the geography lens gives the posting as spanning 1956 to 1959. Month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: The Chilean army lends him to Ecuador to help organize its War Academy at Quito, a posting of several years at nine thousand feet. It is his first long service abroad and his first experience of being the instructing power rather than the instructed. The continental officer class is one guild with local chapters, and a Chilean major teaching staff doctrine in the Andes is doing that guild's ordinary work. Nineteen years later the same guild will meet in Santiago and agree, in writing, to hunt each other's exiles.
suggested_refs: The Academia de Guerra of Ecuador at Quito, organized with Chilean assistance in the late 1950s

stops.name: Antofagasta, the 1st Division in the Atacama
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: He takes a staff post with the 1st Army Division at Antofagasta, in the driest desert on earth, a young officer learning the terrain of a garrison command he does not yet know he will need. In October 1973 a helicopter will come through this same division's ground shooting prisoners, and this division's commander will count them. The Caravan of Death starts here, in a desert whose very emptiness, no witnesses, no water, no cover, makes it useful for exactly that.
suggested_refs: che_guevara.journey.json, the night at Baquedano, 1952
The 1st Army Division headquarters at Antofagasta

stops.name: Santiago, the Academia de Guerra and the writing of Geopolítica
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the sub-directorship; month and day defaulted. The coordinate is described in the verified pool as an approximation of the Providencia-area academy site.
stops.campa: Named sub-director of the Academia de Guerra, he teaches military geography and geopolitics to the officers who will be his colonels in 1973. Out of these classes comes Geopolítica, published in 1968 while he is a colonel: a textbook synthesis holding that a state is an organism competing for space and that its frontiers are lines of pressure. It circulates in military academies across South America, in Brazilian translation among others. He is by now a writer of manuals, which is a slower form of authority than command and outlasts it.
suggested_refs: Geopolítica, Santiago 1968; no copy was opened for this file and its doctrine is described at second hand
sources: standard biographical accounts of the pre-1973 career

stops.name: Santiago, the garrison of the capital
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1971; day defaulted. The 1968 appointments are recorded inconsistently in the pool, as chief of staff of the 2nd Division at Santiago and as command of the 6th Division at Iquique 1968-1971; both come from the same source and are not reconciled.
stops.campa: Division general, he is named General Commander of the Santiago Army Garrison, and the following year General Chief of Staff of the Army. Salvador Allende has been president since November 1970 and the Popular Unity government is nationalizing copper by unanimous vote of a congress that will shortly turn on it. The garrison command puts Pinochet in charge of the troops in the capital during the years the capital comes apart: the strikes, the queues, the marches counter-marching down the same avenue. He is regarded, correctly for the moment, as a constitutionalist.
suggested_refs: The Santiago Army Garrison command post; the exact address is unverified

stops.name: Santiago, Allende hands him the army
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: General Carlos Prats resigns as commander-in-chief after the officer corps and their wives turn against him in public, and Allende appoints Pinochet in his place. The president chooses him because he is the senior general, because he has no political history that anyone can name, and because Prats vouches for him personally. Chile is by then near collapse: the road haulage struck, the chamber of deputies in declared revolt against the executive, the streets divided block by block. Nineteen days remain. Pinochet gives the president who appointed him no warning at all.
suggested_refs: The resignation of Carlos Prats, 23 August 1973, and the appointment that followed the same day

stops.name: La Moneda, the palace burns
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At dawn the navy takes Valparaíso; by midday Hawker Hunters of the air force are putting rockets into the Palacio de La Moneda while the president broadcasts from inside it. Allende dies in the burning building. This is the same seat of government where Bernardo O'Higgins was proclaimed Supreme Director in 1817, and the fire of this morning destroys the original Acta de la Independencia de Chile, the document that founded the republic he led. The republic's founding paper and its elected president burn on one September morning in one room.
stops.quote: las Fuerzas Armadas y de orden han actuado en el día de hoy sólo bajo la inspiración patriótica de sacar al país del caos que en forma aguda lo estaba precipitando el Gobierno marxista de Salvador Allende
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, broadcast address of 11 September 1973, transcribed from the TVN 24 Horas archive; no primary tape was consulted for this file
suggested_refs: ohiggins.journey.json, the Acta de la Independencia lost in the fire of La Moneda, 1973
The bombardment of La Moneda, 11 September 1973

stops.name: Diego Portales, the junta takes a building
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1973 for the move; the day is given as the day of the coup.
stops.campa: With La Moneda gutted, the junta of the four commanders, army, navy, air force and Carabineros, installs its government in the Diego Portales building on the Alameda: a modernist slab raised two years earlier for a United Nations conference under Allende, built at speed by volunteer labour. The socialist government's conference hall becomes the dictatorship's cabinet room. The junta governs from here until the rebuilt palace reopens in 1981 and keeps the tower for its legislative work until 1990. The building is now a cultural centre named for Gabriela Mistral.
suggested_refs: The Edificio Diego Portales, Alameda 227, now the Centro Cultural Gabriela Mistral

stops.name: Dawson Island, the cabinet at the end of the world
stops.date_confidence: attested. The COMPINGIM camp operates from 11 September 1973; the second camp, Río Chico, opens 20 December 1973 and runs to September 1974.
stops.campa: Ministers and senior officials of the fallen government are flown to Dawson Island in the Strait of Magellan and put to work in two camps, COMPINGIM near Puerto Harris from the day of the coup and Río Chico from December. It is the coldest inhabited latitude in the republic, chosen for the reason the Salesians once chose it for the Selk'nam: nobody leaves. The cabinet of a constitutional government breaks rock and lays pipe at the bottom of the continent while Santiago is told on the radio that the country has been saved from chaos.
suggested_refs: Sergio Bitar, Isla 10, the testimony of a Dawson Island internee

stops.name: Estadio Nacional, the terraces
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool dates the stadium's use to September and November 1973 without a start day; the stop takes the day after the coup as its entry point. The pool also carries two coordinates for the stadium, 55 m apart, and that divergence is left standing.
stops.campa: The national stadium in Ñuñoa, built for the 1962 World Cup, is turned into a holding pen. Thousands pass through the terraces and the changing rooms in the weeks after the coup; they are sorted, interrogated in the velodrome, and in documented cases killed. The Rettig Commission will name what happened here seventeen years later. In 2003 the ground is declared a national monument and a section of the old wooden terrace is left unrestored, so that the place where Chile played football keeps the physical evidence of the same September.
suggested_refs: The preserved Escotilla 8 terrace section, Estadio Nacional, declared a national monument in 2003

stops.name: Pisagua, the nitrate port reopened
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool gives the camp's operation as 1973-1974 without a start date; the day here is a declared default and carries no evidentiary weight.
stops.campa: The abandoned nitrate port of Pisagua, a handful of wooden buildings under a cliff on the Atacama coast, is reopened as a concentration camp for political prisoners. The regime does not have to invent its geography of confinement. It inherits it: the same buildings held prisoners under Ibáñez in the 1920s and again in 1948, when the Communist Party was outlawed and its militants shipped north. Twenty years after the coup a mass grave will be opened in the dunes above the town and the bodies will come out of the dry salt ground recognizable.
suggested_refs: The Pisagua camp and the mass grave found in the salt ground above the town in 1990

stops.name: Cerro Chena, the garrison does its own killing
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1973; day defaulted. The verified pool attributed these killings to Arellano Stark's flying column; that attribution is withdrawn, since the column travelled by helicopter northward from Cauquenes and never operated at San Bernardo.
stops.campa: At the Cerro Chena garrison in San Bernardo, on the ground of the Infantry School where he served as a lieutenant thirty years before, prisoners are held in an underground gallery and executed. No travelling column comes here. The local garrison does its own killing, in the same weeks and by the same method as the helicopter working the north. What Arellano carries from town to town is a demonstration, put on for the officer corps, of a practice already general in the army.
suggested_refs: The Cerro Chena case, prosecuted separately from the Caravan of Death
sources: Patricia Verdugo, 'Chile, Pinochet, and the Caravan of Death'

stops.name: Antofagasta, General Lagos counts fifty-six
stops.date_confidence: attested. The Caravan itself runs 30 September to 22 October 1973, so the month label of October carried in the pool understates its start. The toll is contested and left contested: at least 75 per the BBC and army custody figures, 97 per Memoria y Justicia.
stops.campa: General Sergio Arellano Stark, carrying a written appointment from Pinochet as Official Delegate of the Commander-in-Chief, has been travelling the country by Puma helicopter since the end of September, taking prisoners out of military jails and shooting them. On the nineteenth of October General Joaquín Lagos, commanding the 1st Division here, tallies fifty-six dead in his own zone and goes to Pinochet to say so. The tally is what grounds the helicopter. The bodies from the northern towns are buried unmarked or dropped into the sea.
suggested_refs: The Lagos tally of 19 October 1973, presented to Pinochet at Antofagasta

stops.name: Londres 38, the founding of DINA
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1973 for the founding of DINA; day defaulted. The house at Londres 38 is in use from 1973 to 1975.
stops.campa: The Dirección de Inteligencia Nacional is founded under Colonel Manuel Contreras, answerable to Pinochet personally and to nobody else, not to the junta and not to the army. Among its first houses is a narrow building at Londres 38, in the downtown street of Spanish-named houses behind the church of San Francisco, five minutes' walk from La Moneda. Prisoners arrive blindfolded and cannot say afterwards where they were held, only that they climbed one step and heard a heavy door. The address is a memorial now and the paving carries the names.
suggested_refs: Londres 38, espacio de memorias; the named paving stones of the street

stops.name: Villa Grimaldi, Cuartel Terranova
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1974 for the start; month and day defaulted. DINA runs the site 1974-1976 and it passes to the CNI on DINA's dissolution; the 1974-1978 span carried in the pool attributes two extra years of DINA control.
stops.campa: DINA takes over a walled estate in Peñalolén at the foot of the cordillera, an old country house with a rose garden that had lately been a restaurant and a meeting place for Santiago's bohemia. It becomes Cuartel Terranova, the largest of the secret centres. When DINA is dissolved the CNI inherits the place. Before leaving power the regime demolishes the buildings and hauls away the rubble, which is a confession in the form of a bulldozer. The rose garden survives.
suggested_refs: Cuartel Terranova, demolished by the regime before 1990; the surviving rose garden

stops.name: Colonia Dignidad, the colony on the Perquilauquén
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool gives the site's use as 1973-1990; month and day defaulted to the start of 1974. The coordinate is a correction of about 50 km against the figure the pool originally carried.
stops.campa: In the interior of the Parral commune, on the Perquilauquén river, a closed German settlement founded by the lay preacher Paul Schäfer keeps its own airstrip, its own hospital, its own armoury and its own children. DINA uses it as a detention and interrogation site, and the colony's members hold prisoners the state does not admit to holding. The arrangement suits both parties exactly: a sect answerable to no Chilean authority, and a secret police that wants a place outside the country's law and inside the country's borders.
suggested_refs: Colonia Dignidad, now Villa Baviera, interior of the Parral commune near Catillo
sources: German and Chilean judicial investigations into Colonia Dignidad

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the car bomb for Carlos Prats
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool dates the Prats assassination to 1974 without month or day; the day is a declared default and carries no evidentiary weight.
stops.campa: Carlos Prats, the general Pinochet replaced and the man who vouched for him to Allende, is living in exile in Buenos Aires and writing his memoirs. A DINA bomb under his car kills him and his wife Sofía Cuthbert. Argentina is governed that year by Isabel Perón, whose husband had come home only the year before from eighteen years of exile at the Quinta 17 de Octubre in Puerta de Hierro. The killing settles the question of DINA's reach. Its business is Chileans, wherever on earth they have gone.
suggested_refs: juan_peron.journey.json and eva_peron.journey.json, the Puerta de Hierro years
The Prats assassination, Buenos Aires, 1974

stops.name: Santiago, Supreme Chief and then President
stops.date_confidence: attested. Two events merged: proclaimed Supreme Chief of the Nation on 17 June 1974 and formally titled President of the Republic on 17 December 1974; the stop takes the later date.
stops.campa: In June the junta proclaims him Supreme Chief of the Nation; in December he takes the title President of the Republic. The three other commanders remain, in form, his equals, and for six more years the fiction of a collegial government is maintained. In practice the decrees are signed by one man and the intelligence service reports to one man. The republic he now presides over has no congress, no legal parties and no electoral roll, the rolls having been burned. He is fifty-nine and has commanded the army for sixteen months.
stops.quote: El país está tranquilo, porque disponemos de un buen servicio de inteligencia
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, speech of September 1974, reported in Las Últimas Noticias; reached only through a Chilean press compilation, no primary transcript located
suggested_refs: Decree-law 806 of 17 December 1974, conferring the title President of the Republic
sources: Las Últimas Noticias, September 1974, via the LaMula compilation

stops.name: Academia de Guerra, the founding act of Condor
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Manuel Contreras convenes the intelligence chiefs of Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay at the Army War Academy in Santiago, the building where Pinochet taught geopolitics twelve years earlier, and they sign the founding act of Operation Condor. The agreement is short and clear: each service may hunt its own exiles on the others' territory, and each will hand over what it catches. The continental officers' guild that lent a Chilean major to Quito in 1956 now keeps a shared filing system for the disappeared.
stops.quote: Yo me voy a morir...pero elecciones no habrá
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, 17 June 1975, in La Nación (Chile), Las frases para el bronce de Pinochet, 11 December 2006
suggested_refs: The founding act of Operation Condor, Academia de Guerra, Santiago, 25 November 1975
sources: declassified US State Department cables on Operation Condor

stops.name: Sheridan Circle, the bomb in Washington
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date. The coordinate is supplied from outside the verified pool, which carries no Washington pin for this killing, and should be treated as a reconstruction until pinned.
stops.campa: Orlando Letelier, Allende's ambassador to Washington and his last defence minister, is driving down Massachusetts Avenue through Sheridan Circle when a bomb under the driver's seat detonates. He dies, and so does Ronni Moffitt, the young American colleague riding beside him. The device was placed by Michael Townley, a DINA agent, on orders relayed from Contreras's deputy Pedro Espinoza. Condor has now killed in the capital of the country that helped bring the junta in, fourteen blocks from the White House, on an avenue of embassies.
suggested_refs: The Letelier and Moffitt memorial at Sheridan Circle, Massachusetts Avenue, Washington

stops.name: Cerro Chacarillas, the timetable
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On a hill inside the Parque Metropolitano, before a torchlit rally of the regime's youth movement, Pinochet reads out a timetable: recovery, then transition, then what he calls a protected democracy with the armed forces retained as guarantor. The Chacarillas speech is the first admission that the regime intends to end and the first proof that it intends to write the terms of its own ending. A year later the air force general Gustavo Leigh, who says publicly that the transition should be faster, is forced into retirement and the junta of equals is finished.
suggested_refs: The Chacarillas speech of 9 July 1977 and its schedule for a protected democracy

stops.name: Santiago, the plebiscite of 1980
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Seven years to the day after the coup, a plebiscite is held on a constitution written by the regime's own jurists. There are no electoral rolls, no opposition campaign and no independent count; the official result is 67.04 per cent in favour. The text creates a senate with appointed members, a national security council with a military majority, and a seat for life for former presidents. The economists trained at Chicago have already rebuilt the country on the matching principle: property first, and the vote afterwards, if at all.
stops.quote: hacer de Chile una nación de propietarios y no de proletarios
stops.quote_source: Declaración de Principios del Gobierno de Chile, Junta de Gobierno, March 1974, as quoted in Chilean scholarship. English Wikiquote assigns the same formulation to a speech of 24 April 1987; the conflict is unresolved and the line may not be a personal utterance at all.
suggested_refs: The 1980 Constitution of Chile, drafted by the Ortúzar Commission
sources: Junta de Gobierno, Declaración de Principios, 1974

stops.name: Viña del Mar, the summer palace at Cerro Castillo
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool gives no date for the residence, which is in continuous use across 1973-1990; 1983 is a declared placeholder chosen to sit in the year of the first national protests and carries no evidentiary weight of its own.
stops.campa: The presidential palace on the hill above Viña del Mar, the summer seat of Chilean governments since 1930, holds the executive through the hot months. He is by now Capitán General, a rank held in the republic's history only by Bernardo O'Higgins in 1817 and Ramón Freire in 1823, granted to him in 1982; the founder's title and the founder's palace, taken in the same decade. From this coast he watches the copper price collapse and the peso with it, and the middle class that welcomed the coup come out into the street banging saucepans.
stops.quote: Esta nunca ha sido dictadura, señores, esta es dictablanda, pero si es necesario, vamos a tener que apretar la mano
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, 2 September 1983, quoted in El Mercurio, 11 December 2006. The word dictablanda is not his coinage; it is Spanish, popularized in 1930 for the government of Dámaso Berenguer.
suggested_refs: ohiggins.journey.json, the rank of Capitán General held by the founder in 1817
The Palacio Presidencial de Cerro Castillo, Callao 398, Viña del Mar
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Palacio Presidencial de Cerro Castillo'

stops.name: Cuesta Las Achupallas, the ambush in the canyon
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date. The place is a correction: the verified pool located the ambush at El Melocotón, which is Pinochet's country house some 20 km further up the canyon and the point the motorcade was returning from.
stops.campa: Returning to Santiago from his country house at El Melocotón, the presidential motorcade climbs the Cuesta Las Achupallas in the Cajón del Maipo, between La Obra and Las Vertientes, and drives into an ambush laid by the Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front. Rockets are fired at the cars at close range. Five bodyguards are killed and eleven wounded; a rocket strikes his own vehicle and fails to detonate. He is driven out with a cut hand and shows the bandage on television that night. The year that follows is the bloodiest of the regime's second decade.
stops.quote: Tengo la cara agria, por eso tal vez dicen que soy un dictador
suggested_refs: The FPMR ambush of 7 September 1986 at the Cuesta Las Achupallas, Cajón del Maipo

stops.name: Santiago, the night of the No
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Under the timetable written into his own constitution the country votes yes or no on eight more years of Pinochet. Parties have been legal again since the year before; the opposition registers voters house by house, takes the fifteen minutes of late-night television the law allows it, and campaigns with a rainbow and a jingle. The No wins with 55.99 per cent. On the night of the count the other commanders refuse to back an annulment. He accepts the result on television the next day, and the clock in his own constitution begins to run against him.
stops.quote: No se mueve ninguna hoja en este país si yo no la estoy moviendo
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, October 1981, in La Nación (Chile), Las frases para el bronce de Pinochet, 11 December 2006; surviving video of the utterance gives a variant opening, Aquí no se mueve una hoja en este país
suggested_refs: The franja televisiva of the 1988 plebiscite campaign, fifteen minutes nightly for each side

stops.name: La Moneda, the handing of the sash
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Patricio Aylwin, who won the December election with about fifty-five per cent, takes the sash at La Moneda and seventeen years of military government end. Six months earlier the outgoing regime had decreed a total prohibition on abortion with no exception of any kind, one of its last acts of legislation. Pinochet does not leave the state on this day. He stays commander-in-chief of the army for eight more years, and his constitution keeps a senate seat waiting for him after that. What changes hands here is the palace, not the guns.
suggested_refs: The transfer of the presidential sash to Patricio Aylwin, La Moneda, 11 March 1990

stops.name: Villa Grimaldi, the Parque por la Paz
stops.date_confidence: attested. The pool gave 1994, which appears to come from informal public access to the site three years before the formal inauguration of 22 March 1997.
stops.campa: The Parque por la Paz Villa Grimaldi is inaugurated on the ground of Cuartel Terranova, a year and a half before the arrest in London and while he still commands the army. Survivors and the families of the disappeared lay out the paths themselves over the foundations of the buildings the regime demolished, marking in tile and outline the rooms that are no longer standing. Chile spends the 1990s doing this quietly, site by site, with no help from the state and no verdict from any court. The map of the dictatorship is drawn by the people who were held on it.
suggested_refs: Parque por la Paz Villa Grimaldi, inaugurated 22 March 1997, Peñalolén
sources: Villa Grimaldi Peace Park institutional history

stops.name: Valparaíso, the seat for life
stops.date_confidence: attested. Two dates the pool had collapsed into one: he retires as commander-in-chief on 10 March 1998 and is sworn in as senator on 11 March. The stop takes the swearing-in.
stops.campa: He hands over the army on the tenth of March and is sworn in as senator for life on the eleventh, in the concrete congress building the regime itself planted in Valparaíso, away from Santiago, to hold the legislature at arm's length from the capital. Deputies stand in the chamber holding photographs of the disappeared while he takes his seat. The immunity that comes with the seat is the reason for the seat. Within seven months a magistrate in Madrid will test what that immunity is worth outside Chile.
stops.quote: La única solución para el problema de los derechos humanos es el olvido
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, 21 September 1995, reported by Agencia DPA and carried in two independent Chilean compilations
suggested_refs: The Congreso Nacional in the El Almendral district of Valparaíso, built under the 1980 constitution

stops.name: The London Clinic, the arrest in the private room
stops.date_confidence: attested. The verified pool carried three different coordinates for this one building across two lenses; the figure used here is the correction that reconciles them.
stops.campa: Recovering from back surgery in a private room at the London Clinic, on the corner of Devonshire Place and Marylebone Road, Pinochet is served with a provisional arrest warrant issued through Bow Street. The Spanish judge Baltasar Garzón wants him extradited for the torture and disappearance of Spanish citizens, and works from Madrid, invoking a doctrine of universal jurisdiction that most governments had never seen tested. A former head of state is arrested in a third country for what he did in his own. It has not happened before.
suggested_refs: juan_peron.journey.json, the Madrid exile at Puerta de Hierro
R v Bow Street Metropolitan Stipendiary Magistrate, ex parte Pinochet, the case name taken from the court that issued the warrant

stops.name: Wentworth Estate, the golf-course detention
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool gives the detention as spanning October 1998 to March 2000 without a date for the move to Surrey; the day is a declared default. Duration is contested: sixteen months counting arrest to release, eighteen in one source, and sixteen is used.
stops.campa: For most of sixteen months he lives under guard in a rented house on the Wentworth Estate at Virginia Water in Surrey, a golf-course suburb of gated drives and clipped verges. Chilean supporters bring him food and flags at the entrance; Chilean exiles who fled his police in the 1970s picket the same entrance from the other side of the road. Margaret Thatcher comes and takes tea with him. He is eighty-three, and for the first time since 1973 his movements are decided by somebody else.
stops.quote: Yo sólo era un aspirante a dictador, nunca fui un verdadero dictador
stops.quote_source: Pinochet in London detention, November 1998, in La Nación (Chile), Las frases para el bronce de Pinochet, 11 December 2006
suggested_refs: The Wentworth Estate, Virginia Water, Borough of Runnymede; the exact house is not identified in reachable sources

stops.name: House of Lords, the line drawn at 1988
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool gives March 1999 without a day; defaulted to the first. The pool also flags that secondary summaries compress the three hearings inconsistently, and that compression is not resolved here.
stops.campa: The Lords hear the immunity question three times. The first panel strips immunity by three votes to two; that judgment is set aside when it emerges that one of the majority had undisclosed ties to Amnesty International, the first time in modern English law that a decision of the highest court is vacated for apparent bias. The rehearing before seven judges holds that a former head of state has no immunity for torture, but only for acts after 1988, when the United Kingdom brought the Torture Convention into its own law. The charge sheet shrinks from hundreds to a handful.
suggested_refs: R v Bow Street Metropolitan Stipendiary Magistrate, ex parte Pinochet (No 3), the rehearing before seven law lords
sources: R v Bow Street Metropolitan Stipendiary Magistrate, ex parte Pinochet

stops.name: Queen Anne's Gate, the home secretary decides
stops.date_confidence: attested. Straw signalled the health finding in January 2000 and authorized release on 2 March; the stop takes the March date. The building is a correction: the Home Office was at 50 Queen Anne's Gate until 2005, so the Marsham Street address carried in the pool is anachronistic for these events.
stops.campa: Jack Straw, home secretary, decides that Pinochet is medically unfit to stand trial and will not be extradited to Spain, and authorizes his release. The decision is taken at the Home Office in Queen Anne's Gate, the department's headquarters until its move to Marsham Street five years later. Four countries had asked for him. A neurological report obtained in January had found him impaired; the report is disputed by the Spanish and Belgian governments, and by doctors who had never examined him, and it is not published.
suggested_refs: The Home Office at 50 Queen Anne's Gate, SW1, the department's seat in 1998-2000

stops.name: Pudahuel, out of the wheelchair
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The air force jet lands at Pudahuel and he is wheeled down onto the tarmac, where the commander-in-chief of the army and a crowd of supporters are waiting with a band. He rises from the wheelchair unaided, straightens, and walks. The photograph goes around the world within the hour and destroys, as an argument, the medical case that brought him home. Chilean judges who have been told for two years that this man cannot follow a question read the same newspapers as everybody else.
suggested_refs: The photographs of the arrival at Pudahuel, 3 March 2000

stops.name: Santiago, the immunity stripped and the indictment
stops.date_confidence: attested. Two events merged: the Santiago Court of Appeal strips his senatorial immunity on 23 May 2000 and Judge Juan Guzmán Tapia indicts him on 1 December 2000; the stop takes the indictment.
stops.campa: In May the Santiago Court of Appeal strips his senatorial immunity in the Caravan of Death case; on the first of December Judge Juan Guzmán Tapia indicts him for the kidnapping of seventy-five opponents. The charge is kidnapping and not murder, because a body never found is, in Chilean law, a person still being held. The amnesty the regime wrote for itself in 1978 covers completed crimes. A disappearance is never completed. The legal fiction built to hide the dead is turned around and used to open the files.
stops.quote: ¿A quién le vamos a pedir perdón? ¿A los que trataron de matarnos? ¿A los que trataron de liquidar a la Patria?
stops.quote_source: Pinochet, 11 September 1994, reported by Agencia DPA; also cited in Sandrine Lefranc, Políticas del perdón, Universitat de València, 2004, p. 164
suggested_refs: The Guzmán indictment of 1 December 2000 and the kidnapping doctrine that defeats the 1978 amnesty

stops.name: Santiago, the dementia finding
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 2002; day defaulted.
stops.campa: The Supreme Court dismisses the Caravan indictment, holding that a vascular dementia leaves him unfit to stand trial. He resigns his senate seat and the prosecutions stop. For two years the settled position of the Chilean state is that its former ruler cannot follow a legal argument. The finding is reached on medical evidence and lands as a political settlement: no conviction, no acquittal, no further questions. A considerable part of the country wants exactly that and says so at the ballot box.
suggested_refs: The Supreme Court ruling of July 2002 on fitness to stand trial

stops.name: Santiago, the finding revoked
stops.date_confidence: attested. The pool credited the fitness ruling to Judge Guzmán; the actor is corrected. The Santiago Court of Appeals revokes the dementia finding 14-9 on 28 May 2004, and Guzmán then indicts in the Operation Condor case and orders house arrest in December 2004.
stops.campa: The Santiago Court of Appeals revokes the dementia finding by fourteen votes to nine and strips his immunity again. What moves the judges is not new medicine but a television interview he gave to a Miami station, lucid, aggrieved and self-justifying, from an armchair. In December Guzmán indicts him in the Operation Condor case and puts him under house arrest. The shape of his last years is fixed by this reversal: immunity lifted, indictment, appeal, immunity restored, and the clock running out on every one of them.
suggested_refs: The Santiago Court of Appeals ruling of 28 May 2004, decided 14-9
sources: Wikipedia, 'Indictment and arrest of Augusto Pinochet'

stops.name: Washington, the Riggs accounts
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 2004 for the Senate report; day defaulted. The coordinate for the bank is supplied from outside the verified pool and should be treated as a reconstruction until pinned. The sum is contested inside the pool between four to eight million and six to eight million; the lower range is used.
stops.campa: A United States Senate subcommittee reports that Riggs Bank, the Washington house that held the accounts of presidents and embassies, helped Pinochet hide between four and eight million dollars behind shell companies and false variants of his own name while his assets stood under court freeze. The bank's officers had invited him to open the accounts in 1994. Riggs pleads guilty, pays sixteen million in fines and nine million to his victims. The money does what the bodies could not do: it turns his own supporters against him.
suggested_refs: US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, report on Riggs Bank, 2004
sources: US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, 2004

stops.name: Santiago, the last house arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A Chilean court orders him held at home again. He is ninety-one and faces roughly three hundred open charges for killing, torture, kidnapping, tax evasion and embezzlement, and his wife and five children are moving toward indictment over the Riggs accounts. Three days earlier, on his birthday, Lucía Hiriart read out a written statement in which he accepted political responsibility for everything that had been done. It is not offered as a confession and no court treats it as one. He will be dead in twelve days, convicted of nothing at all.
stops.quote: Asumo la responsabilidad política de todo lo obrado
stops.quote_source: Written statement of 25 November 2006, read aloud by Lucía Hiriart; fuller text reported in the Washington Post, 26 November 2006
suggested_refs: The birthday statement of 25 November 2006 and its careful phrase, responsabilidad política

stops.name: Hospital Militar, the tenth of December
stops.date_confidence: attested. The coordinate is a correction: the afterlife lens of the pool marked the death at the Santiago centroid, seven kilometres from the hospital.
stops.campa: He dies of heart failure at the Military Hospital in La Reina, a week after a heart attack, on the tenth of December, which is International Human Rights Day. Two crowds gather in Santiago that afternoon: one outside the hospital, weeping and singing the national anthem, and one in the Alameda, uncorking bottles in the street. The state that could not decide for sixteen years what to do with him is spared the decision. No court in any country ever reached a verdict on Augusto Pinochet.
suggested_refs: The Hospital Militar de Santiago, La Reina; the death certificate of 10 December 2006

stops.name: Escuela Militar, the funeral the state does not attend
stops.date_confidence: attested. The coordinate is a correction of about 1.2 km against the figure carried in the pool.
stops.campa: President Michelle Bachelet, whose father died under torture by his own air force in 1974 and who was herself held at Villa Grimaldi, refuses a state funeral. The army holds a ceremony at the Military School in Las Condes for a former commander-in-chief and not for a former head of state, and the cabinet is ordered to stay away. Tens of thousands file past the coffin over two days. A grandson gives a defiant speech from the platform and is stripped of his commission for it within the week.
suggested_refs: The military honours at the Escuela Militar, Los Militares 4500, Las Condes, 12 December 2006
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Escuela Militar del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins'

stops.name: Los Boldos, the ashes in a private house
stops.date_confidence: the verified pool dates the deposit of the ashes to December 2006 without a day; 13 December follows the ceremony of the twelfth. The Los Boldos estate itself is not pinned in any reachable source and the coordinate is the Santo Domingo commune centroid, a declared placeholder.
stops.campa: The body is cremated rather than buried and the ashes are taken to the family's estate at Los Boldos, on the coast south of San Antonio, and kept in the house. There is no grave. A tomb would be desecrated inside a week, and a tomb would also be a shrine. No public statue of him stands anywhere in Chile, and his most durable mark on the map is the network his opponents built on the sites he used. He is born on this coast at Valparaíso and ends on it, at an address the state does not administer.
suggested_refs: The Los Boldos estate, Santo Domingo; not pinned in any reachable source
The absence of any standing public monument to Pinochet in Chile, a reconstruction from documented absence rather than a citation
